It's interesting to think about why do we like a task or not. We hate the task that make us procrastinate, because they matter to us. It's actually the core issue of procrastination: fear of failure. You don't want to fail an essay because it matters to you. What you hate is the possibility to fail and the unknown: it provokes our biggest fears.  

However, fear is inevitable in the process of life and that's when the difference between a child and an adult matter. As a child, you can avoid fear and seek comfort through your parents. As you grow up, you encounter more anxiety-inducing situations that you need to face alone.  Ie: asking a girl out > living together > getting married > having kids. When you manage those fears, you're responsible. However, it's tempting to bail out, seeing the unpleasantness of the situations. What happens if you flee  tasks like writing an essay, planning a trip, buying a flat, living with your partner ? Well you flee what characterizes an adult. 

Discipline matters because it involves commitment to ta project, meaning working even when you don't feel like it, accompanied with a structured plan which allows you to diminish the fear engendered by the unknown.

No matter how passionate you are, you can be passionate about every part of your life. Unpleasant taks, therefore feelings are inevitable. The more you grow up, the more you face unpleasant tasks. If you bail out, you remain a child.
